attrs.title: Signs your Meta tracking is missing sales
attrs.lead: Meta can only optimise towards the conversions it sees. These are the problems we find most often.

items.title: Meta shows far fewer purchases than your store
items.text:
The Pixel runs in the browser, so ad blockers, iPhone privacy settings and short cookies hide a share of your sales. Meta then thinks your ads work worse than they do, and learns from fewer buyers.

We add the Conversions API, which sends purchases from your server or store. Together with the Pixel, Meta sees close to every sale, and your reported results match your store far more closely.

items.title: Purchases are counted twice
items.text:
When the Pixel and the Conversions API both send a purchase without the same event ID, Meta counts both. Results look great, but they’re wrong, and bidding chases sales that never happened.

We send one event ID with both versions of every event, so Meta keeps one. Then we check the deduplication rate in Events Manager and compare purchases with your store.

items.title: Event match quality is “Poor” or “OK”
items.text:
Event match quality shows how well Meta can link an event to a person. With low scores, Meta can’t tell who bought, so it can’t find more people like them.

We send hashed customer data with each event: email, phone, name, city and Meta’s click and browser IDs, with consent. Scores usually rise to “Good” or “Great”.

items.title: Tracking stopped after a site change
items.text:
A new theme, checkout app or cookie banner can quietly remove events. Campaigns keep spending while Meta sees nothing, and nobody notices for days.

We rebuild the events on the current site, test them, and set an alert if purchases stop arriving, so a site change can’t break tracking silently again.

items.title: You’re not sure the Conversions API is even on
items.text:
Many stores switched on an app or plugin years ago and never checked it. Some send only page views, some send purchases without values, and some stopped working long ago.

We check every event in Events Manager: where it comes from, what data it carries and whether it matches your store. Then we fix what’s missing and write it all down.

items.title: Leads from your CRM never reach Meta
items.text:
For lead generation, Meta only knows someone filled in a form. It never learns which leads became customers, so it keeps finding cheap leads that don’t buy.

We send CRM stages back through the Conversions API, such as qualified, booked and won, so Meta can optimise for leads that turn into revenue.

What we set up

Eight parts of Meta tracking, set up and tested

For each one: why it matters, what we set up, what we usually find and what you get.

Area 1 of 8

Pixel events

The Pixel still matters: it sees browsing behaviour and sends events quickly. It just can’t see everything on its own.

What we set up

  • Base code on every page
  • Standard events
  • Value, currency and content IDs
  • Custom conversions
  • One Pixel per business
  • Test events

What we usually find

  • ! Two Pixels on the same site
  • ! Purchase firing on page reload
  • ! No value on purchases
  • ! Events from an old theme

What you get

  • One clean Pixel
  • Standard events in the right places
  • Values and content IDs on every purchase
  • Old events removed

Area 2 of 8

Conversions API

The Conversions API sends events from your server or store, so blocked browsers and short cookies don’t hide them.

What we set up

  • Shopify or WordPress integration
  • Conversions API gateway
  • Server-side Tag Manager
  • Events sent from the server
  • Access token and security
  • Error monitoring

What we usually find

  • ! An app switched on but sending nothing
  • ! Only page views sent from the server
  • ! An expired access token
  • ! Errors in Events Manager nobody saw

What you get

  • The right connection for your platform
  • Key events sent from the server
  • Errors checked and fixed
  • An alert if events stop

Area 3 of 8

Deduplication

With both the Pixel and the Conversions API on, every event arrives twice. Without the same event ID, Meta counts both.

Deduplication

Purchase event

  • Before398402800
  • After396404412

What we set up

  • Event ID on Pixel events
  • Same ID on server events
  • Event names that match
  • Timing
  • Deduplication rate
  • Purchases vs orders

What we usually find

  • ! No event IDs at all
  • ! Different IDs on each side
  • ! Event names that don’t match
  • ! Twice as many purchases as orders

What you get

  • One event ID shared by both
  • Matching event names
  • Deduplication checked in Events Manager
  • Purchases that match your orders

Area 4 of 8

Event match quality

The more Meta can match events to people, the better it targets and reports. Customer data, sent safely, is the key.

What we set up

  • Hashed email and phone
  • Name, city and country
  • Click ID (fbc) and browser ID (fbp)
  • External ID
  • IP and user agent
  • Consent

What we usually find

  • ! No customer data sent
  • ! Email sent unhashed
  • ! Click ID lost on redirects
  • ! Data sent without consent

What you get

  • Hashed customer data with every event
  • Click and browser IDs kept
  • Consent respected
  • Scores of “Good” or “Great”

Area 5 of 8

Domain and event setup

Domain verification shows Meta the site is yours, and event priority decides what counts for iPhone users who opt out.

What we set up

  • Domain verification
  • Aggregated event measurement
  • Event priority
  • Checkout on other domains
  • Subdomains
  • Business portfolio ownership

What we usually find

  • ! Domain never verified
  • ! Purchase not the top-priority event
  • ! Checkout on a domain Meta can’t see
  • ! Pixel owned by a former agency

What you get

  • Domain verified
  • Events prioritised by value
  • Checkout domains covered
  • Pixel owned by your business

Area 6 of 8

Consent and privacy

Tracking must respect your cookie banner and privacy laws, or events go missing in some places and break the rules in others.

What we set up

  • Cookie banner and consent mode
  • Which events need consent
  • Hashing before sending
  • Data processing terms
  • Privacy policy
  • Country rules

What we usually find

  • ! The Pixel firing before consent
  • ! The banner blocking everything, including the server side
  • ! Unhashed data sent
  • ! Privacy policy not mentioning Meta

What you get

  • Events that follow your banner
  • Data hashed before it leaves your site
  • A privacy policy that covers it
  • Settings checked for each market

Area 7 of 8

CRM and offline events

For lead generation, the most useful event happens later: a qualified lead, a booking, a sale. Sending it back teaches Meta which leads matter.

What we set up

  • Lead IDs from forms and lead ads
  • CRM stages: qualified, booked, won
  • Values for each stage
  • HubSpot, Salesforce or Zoho
  • Offline sales
  • Daily or real-time sending

What we usually find

  • ! Meta only sees the form submission
  • ! Lead ad leads never matched to sales
  • ! CRM data exported by hand
  • ! No values on leads

What you get

  • CRM stages sent back to Meta
  • Values on qualified and won leads
  • Campaigns that can optimise for quality
  • No manual exports

Area 8 of 8

Testing and monitoring

Tracking that isn’t tested is a guess. And tracking that isn’t watched breaks with the next site change.

What we set up

  • Test purchases and leads
  • Test events tool
  • Desktop, iPhone and Android
  • Meta vs store or CRM
  • Alerts if events stop
  • A two-week check

What we usually find

  • ! Never tested after setup
  • ! No one checks Events Manager
  • ! Site changes break events silently
  • ! Numbers never compared with the store

What you get

  • Every event tested and recorded
  • Meta compared with your store
  • Alerts when events stop
  • A short checklist for site changes

attrs.label: Need something more custom?
attrs.html:
Need something more custom?

Not every business fits a plugin. If your setup is unusual, tell us what you need. We’ll get on a call, understand the requirement and send you a written quote. Here are custom Conversions API projects we’ve built for other clients.

  • Custom-built or headless stores

    A store built on its own code, or a headless storefront with a separate checkout, where no plugin works.

    What we built: Purchase and checkout events sent from the backend through the Conversions API, with event IDs matched to the browser side.

    • Next.js
    • Laravel
    • Shopify Hydrogen

  • CRM stages and offline sales

    Leads that turn into sales weeks later, in a CRM or over the phone, that Meta never hears about.

    What we built: Qualified, booked and won stages sent back automatically, with values, matched to the original lead.

    • HubSpot
    • Salesforce
    • Zoho

  • Subscriptions and renewals

    A subscription business where the first order is only the start, so Meta undervalues every customer.

    What we built: Sign-ups with a predicted value, and renewals and cancellations sent from payment webhooks.

    • Stripe
    • Recharge
    • Webhooks

  • Bookings, calls and WhatsApp

    Customers who book through a booking system, call, or message on WhatsApp instead of buying online.

    What we built: Bookings, qualified calls and WhatsApp conversations sent as conversion events, with consent.

    • Booking systems
    • Call tracking
    • WhatsApp

  • In-store and point-of-sale purchases

    Shops where people see the ad online but buy in store, so Meta only sees a fraction of the sales.

    What we built: Point-of-sale purchases matched to customers and sent as offline events every day.

    • POS
    • Loyalty data
    • Daily uploads

  • Several brands, countries or Pixels

    One platform running several brands or countries, each with its own Pixel and ad account.

    What we built: Events routed to the right Pixel by brand or country, with one server setup that is easy to maintain.

    • Multi-brand
    • Multi-country
    • Server-side Tag Manager

attrs.title: What it’s like to work with us
Meta Pixel and Conversions API questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: Do I need the Conversions API if I already have the Meta Pixel?
items.answer: Yes, for most businesses. The Pixel runs in the browser and misses conversions because of ad blockers, browser limits and iPhone privacy settings. The Conversions API sends them from your server, and the two together give Meta the most complete picture.

items.question: Why is my Facebook Pixel not tracking purchases?
items.answer: Common causes: the purchase event isn’t on the order confirmation, a theme update removed it, consent settings block it, or checkout happens on another domain. We test and fix each case.

items.question: What is event match quality?
items.answer: A score from 0 to 10 that shows how well Meta can match your events to people. Sending hashed email and phone numbers with events usually raises it.

items.question: How does deduplication work?
items.answer: When the Pixel and the Conversions API send the same event, both include the same event ID. Meta keeps one and discards the duplicate.

items.question: Can you set up CAPI on Shopify or WordPress?
items.answer: Yes. Shopify and WordPress have their own integrations, and for other sites we use server-side Tag Manager or Meta’s gateway.

items.question: Is the Conversions API allowed under privacy laws?
items.answer: Yes, when it respects consent and customer data is hashed before it is sent. We set it up to follow your cookie banner and update your privacy policy where needed.
